    "literal_statement": "Let $\\sigma:{\\mathbb{F}_q}\\rightarrow{\\mathbb{F}_q}$ be a permutation, and let $\\Gamma_\\sigma=\\{(x,\\sigma(x)):x\\in{\\mathbb{F}_q}\\}\\subset{\\mathbb{F}_q}^2$ be its graph. A **collinear triple** is a three-element subset of $\\Gamma_\\sigma$ whose points lie on one affine line. **Collinear-triple conjecture.** For any permutation $\\sigma:{\\mathbb{F}_q}\\rightarrow{\\mathbb{F}_q}$, the number of collinear triples in $\\Gamma_\\sigma$ is at least\n\n$$\n\\frac{q-1}{2}.\n$$\n\nThe source attributes this conjecture to an earlier work and notes that a lower bound of $(q-1)/4$ was already proved there; the stated $(q-1)/2$ bound is presented as the conjectural strengthening.",

    "disposition": "excluded_known_odd_field_result_and_domain_fix",
    "ordinary_attempts": [
      "For odd q, form K_sigma as the union of slope-i lines through (0,sigma(i)). Li gives |K|=q(q+1)/2+sum_e binom(|e|-1,2). The sharp Kakeya bound gives at least (q-1)/2 for this sum; binom(s,3)>=binom(s-1,2) for s>=3 finishes. This is already published, not new.",
      "For the unrestricted literal characteristic-two domain, sigma(x)=x^2 on F_(2^h) has no collinear triple: a nonvertical line meets y=x^2 in at most two points and a vertical line in one. Squaring is a permutation. Thus missing oddness produces an excluded domain correction, not a candidate."
    ],

    "literal_statement": "Let $C$ be a finite or countable graph with no isolated vertices. If $P_{id,w}(1)\\leq 3$, then $|\\operatorname{maxsing}(w)|\\leq 3$.\n2. If $P_{id,w}(1)=3$ and $|\\operatorname{maxsing}(w)|=1$, then there exist integers $a,b$ such that\n\n$$\nP_{id,w}(q)=1+q^a+q^b.\n$$\n\n3. If $P_{id,w}(1)=3$ and $|\\operatorname{maxsing}(w)|=3$, then there is an integer $a$ such that\n\n$$\nP_{id,w}(q)=1+2q^a.\n$$\n\nThe conjecture gives proposed bounds and forms for permutations whose Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial evaluates to at most $3$ at $q=1$.     "title": "Avoidability threshold for powers in odd-difference arithmetic progressions",
    "literal_statement": "Let an infinite word be a sequence over a 4-letter alphabet. An **$r$-power** is a word consisting of repetitions of a nonempty block with exponent $r$, and a word **avoids $r$-powers in arithmetic progressions of odd difference** if no such factor occurs along an arithmetic progression whose common difference is odd. **The power-avoidability conjecture.** For every real number $r<2$, $r$-powers are not avoidable in arithmetic progressions of odd difference over a 4-letter alphabet.     "literal_statement": "Let $G\\cong \\mathbb{Z}/m$ be a finite cyclic group, let $L\\cong\\mathbb{Z}^n$ be a finitely generated free abelian group, let $\\rho\\colon G\\to\\operatorname{aut}_{\\mathbb{Z}}(L)$ be a group homomorphism, and set $\\Gamma=L\\rtimes_{\\rho}G$. The Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence associated to the semidirect product $L\\rtimes_{\\rho}G$ has terms arising from the extension $1\\to L\\to\\Gamma\\to G\\to 1$. **Adem–Ge–Pan–Petrosyan conjecture.** The spectral sequence collapses in the strongest sense: all differentials in the $E_r$-term for $r\\geq 2$ are trivial and all extension problems at the $E_{\\infty}$-level are trivial.       "title": "Conjecture on nonseparating cycle types in nonorientable triangulations",
      "statement": "Let $N_g$ denote the nonorientable surface of Euler genus $g$. If $g \\geq 4$ is even, every triangulation of $N_g$ has a nonseparating cycle that is one-sided and nonorientable-leaving, one that is two-sided and orientable-leaving, and one that is two-sided and nonorientable-leaving.\n\nThe assertion extends the verified low-genus pattern for $N_1$, $N_2$, $N_3$, and $N_4$.
